title: Additive monoidal transport of a finite free module
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be preadditive monoidal categories [def-weil-preadditive-category], [def-sfb-monoidal-category], with finite biproducts and tensor additive in each variable. Let $P:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be additive [def-weil-pbc-additive-functor] and strong monoidal [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor]. Let $R$ be a ring object (a monoid object, [sk-def-sfb-ring-object]), let $M$ be a left internal $R$-module [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], and let $n\geq0$. Use the transported ring $P(R)$ and transported module $P(M)$ of [def-sfb-modobj-transport]. For a ring object $Q$ write $Q^{\oplus n}$ for the biproduct of $n$ copies of its regular module, with the componentwise action; its underlying injections and projections obey $\pi_i\iota_j=\delta_{ij}\mathrm{id}_Q$ and $\sum_i\iota_i\pi_i=\mathrm{id}_{Q^{\oplus n}}$, with empty biproduct $0$.
If $\theta:R^{\oplus n}\xrightarrow{\sim}M$ is an $R$-module isomorphism, there is a $P(R)$-module isomorphism
$$\alpha:P(R)^{\oplus n}\xrightarrow{\sim}P(M).$$
Writing $\iota'_i,\pi'_i$ for the biproduct maps in $\mathcal D$, it satisfies
$$\alpha\iota'_i=P(\theta\iota_i),\qquad \pi'_i\alpha^{-1}=P(\pi_i\theta^{-1}).$$
Thus the transported coordinate and basis maps satisfy the same Kronecker and sum-of-projections identities as the original maps. No braiding, commutativity of $R$, or preservation of a commutative structure by $P$ is required.

proof.text: Use the existing preadditive category of internal modules and its finite biproducts. The transported regular R-module under F = P.mapMod R is definitionally the regular P(R)-module: both actions are the lax tensorator followed by P of multiplication. The existing additive instance for mapMod follows by checking addition on underlying morphisms.

Mathlib Functor.preservesFiniteBiproductsOfAdditive and Functor.mapBiproduct give F(R^n) isomorphic to P(R)^n. Compose the inverse of this isomorphism with F.mapIso theta to obtain alpha. The desc formula for mapBiproduct.inv gives the injection formula. The lift formula for mapBiproduct.hom gives the projection formula, after taking underlying morphisms. Finite biproduct preservation applies also to the empty family.

In Mod C R, simplify (inclusion_j followed by theta.hom) followed by (theta.inv followed by projection_i), cancelling theta.hom followed by theta.inv. The biproduct Kronecker relation gives identity for i=j and zero otherwise. Take underlying morphisms and apply P; functoriality, preservation of identity, and additivity preserving zero give the required transported Kronecker formula.

In Mod C R, distribute composition over the finite sum to rewrite the sum of (theta.inv followed by projection_i) followed by (inclusion_i followed by theta.hom) as theta.inv followed by the biproduct total sum followed by theta.hom. The total sum is identity, and theta.inv followed by theta.hom is identity. Apply the additive composite Mod.forget R followed by P: preservation of finite sums, composition, and identity gives the requested total identity. This calculation includes n=0 without a positivity assumption.

split_report.summary: Expanded finite-free transport into six explicit coordinate steps, using existing module transport and no new nodes. Corrected the ill-typed unbraided commutativity hypothesis by stating the valid monoid-object generality. Checked transported regular actions, both inverse identities, linearity, coordinates and rank zero.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the third sentence of lem-sfb-subfield-flat.proof.md: the additive monoidal inverse image carries the pointwise finite free basis to X. This is the finite-free step (2), third proof paragraph, of sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NO-80e14f5ee (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item in full. The delivery creates no new nodes. I checked it against lem-sfb-subfield-flat.proof.md sentence 3 (main-20261015) and unit sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients clause 2. The statement change is justified: 'commutative ring object' in an unbraided monoidal category is ill-typed (sk-def-sfb-ring-object defines commutativity only when the category is braided), and dropping it strengthens the item without weakening any conclusion. The sole citer, lem-sfb-subfield-flat step 2, supplies exactly the stated hypotheses: strong monoidal, additive, finite biproducts and tensor additive. It uses only the isomorphism F_X≅E_X^n and the coordinate maps, so it stays valid. Step 3 takes from def-sfb-modobj-transport only what its statement says: the transported multiplication and action, and that P of a linear map is linear. Strong monoidal gives the needed lax structure. I checked steps 1, 2 and 4–6 by hand: the componentwise action's unit and associativity laws, linearity of ι_i (which uses id⊗0=0 from tensor additivity), the Kronecker and sum identities after applying P, linearity of finite sums, αβ=id and βα=id, and both coordinate formulas. Rank 0 (P(M) is zero) and rank 1 with P=id also check out. All proof_deps are definitions, so there is no route issue, no tool_uses and no cycle. Grep of dag/nodes and the blueprint for mapMod, finite free and biproduct found no duplicate; lem-sfb-modobj-abelian needs an abelian ambient category. No SGA is cited. No fixes.

lean.statement: theorem monoidalFiniteFreeTransport {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} C] [Preadditive C] [MonoidalCategory C] [HasFiniteBiproducts C] [MonoidalPreadditive C] {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂} D] [Preadditive D] [MonoidalCategory D] [HasFiniteBiproducts D] [MonoidalPreadditive D] (P : C ⥤ D) [P.Additive] [P.Monoidal] (R : C) [MonObj R] (M : Mod C R) (n : ℕ) (θ : (⨁ fun _ : Fin n => Mod.regular R) ≅ M) : ∃ α : (⨁ fun _ : Fin n => Mod.regular (P.obj R)) ≅ (P.mapMod R).obj M, (∀ i : Fin n, (biproduct.ι (fun _ : Fin n => Mod.regular (P.obj R)) i).hom ≫ α.hom.hom = P.map ((biproduct.ι (fun _ : Fin n => Mod.regular R) i).hom ≫ θ.hom.hom)) ∧ (∀ i : Fin n, α.inv.hom ≫ (biproduct.π (fun _ : Fin n => Mod.regular (P.obj R)) i).hom = P.map (θ.inv.hom ≫ (biproduct.π (fun _ : Fin n => Mod.regular R) i).hom)) ∧ (∀ i j : Fin n, P.map ((biproduct.ι (fun _ : Fin n => Mod.regular R) j).hom ≫ θ.hom.hom) ≫ P.map (θ.inv.hom ≫ (biproduct.π (fun _ : Fin n => Mod.regular R) i).hom) = if i = j then 𝟙 (P.obj R) else 0) ∧ (∑ i : Fin n, P.map (θ.inv.hom ≫ (biproduct.π (fun _ : Fin n => Mod.regular R) i).hom) ≫ P.map ((biproduct.ι (fun _ : Fin n => Mod.regular R) i).hom ≫ θ.hom.hom)) = 𝟙 (P.obj M.X)
